topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture structure, learning outcomes, and the multi-step mutation framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic mutations disrupt cell-surface receptor signaling pathways, such as Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinases, to drive sustained proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how differentiation blocks in both hematopoietic lineages and intestinal epithelial crypts contribute to cancer development.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis and p53 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the molecular mechanisms and regulatory balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins that allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and growth-control summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover telomere maintenance, TERT reactivation, p53-mediated stress signaling and senescence, and summarise the growth-control cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss altered cancer metabolism, the Warburg effect, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and the role of metabolic gene mutations and oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction and regulation of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the angiogenic switch, the balance of regulatory factors, and the timing of blood vessel recruitment during tumor progression.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination, efficiency, and genomic characteristics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the multi-step metastatic cascade, the seed and soil hypothesis governing metastatic efficiency, and genomic findings from sequenced metastases.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with closing remarks, recommended reading on updated hallmarks, and housekeeping.
